name: Regex_OpBuildOperandSets
signature: u32 Regex_OpBuildOperandSets(RegexCursor* cursor, RegexValueList** out, RegexCursor* left, RegexCursor* right)
summary: Opcode handler of the pattern VM: allocates a result node, appends one successor-set per instruction operand, then appends the instruction's own character domain to the same node. Returns 0 or 2 (allocation failure).
evidence: The helpers it drives are now merged confident names: Regex_NodeAlloc (0x510E50) for the result node, Regex_BuildSuccessorList for the per-operand walk and Container_Variant_AddChild for the appends; all match the operand/domain bookkeeping described in the body, so the handler role (slot of the opcode table at 0x7AF1B0) is no longer in doubt.

name: Regex_OpBuildOperandSetsSingle
signature: u32 Regex_OpBuildOperandSetsSingle(RegexCursor* cursor, RegexValueList** out, RegexCursor* left, RegexCursor* right)
summary: Single-operand form of Regex_OpBuildOperandSets: when the instruction flag byte at +0xA is zero it pushes the one value from *left, otherwise it walks the operand count and appends each operand's domain before the instruction's own domain.
evidence: Same confident callee set as 0x511774 (Regex_NodeAlloc, Regex_BuildSuccessorList, Container_Variant_AddChild) and the same opcode-table provenance; the body is that handler with the one-operand fast path, so the name only needed the prefix dropped.

name: Regex_OpCopySetAndPush
signature: int Regex_OpCopySetAndPush(RegexCursor* cursor, RegexSet** out, RegexSet** source)
summary: Allocates a result set node, fills it from the instruction through Regex_MatchNode, pushes it into the source list and merges it into the destination set; only reports success when both steps returned 0.
evidence: Regex_NodeAlloc and Regex_MatchNode are confident names now and are called in exactly the allocate/fill/merge order the name implies; Container_Variant_AddChild (0x6E78BC) is the push.

name: Regex_OpPushValueFromRight
signature: u32 Regex_OpPushValueFromRight(RegexCursor* cursor, RegexValueList** out, RegexValueList** left, RegexValueList** right)
summary: Copies the scalar currently held in the right-hand operand list into the output list with tag type 1 and returns 0/2. Mirror image of Regex_OpPushValueFromLeft.
evidence: The generic value-list append is now the confident Container_Variant_AddChild (0x6E7890), and the sibling 0x51203C (same 22-line body reading *left instead of *right) fixes which operand each one copies.

name: Regex_OpPushValueFromLeft
signature: u32 Regex_OpPushValueFromLeft(RegexCursor* cursor, RegexValueList** out, RegexValueList** left, RegexValueList** right)
summary: Copies the scalar held in the left-hand operand list into the output list with tag type 1. Mirror image of Regex_OpPushValueFromRight (0x511FB4).
evidence: Same confident Container_Variant_AddChild append and the same 22-line body as the right-hand twin; the two can only be told apart by which operand pointer they dereference, and the body dereferences *left.

name: Regex_OpPushValueAndVariants
signature: u32 Regex_OpPushValueAndVariants(RegexCursor* cursor, RegexSet** out, RegexSet** value)
summary: Pushes the current value, tagged with the instruction's 16-bit tag, and then pushes one node for each case-fold alternative that 0x513F78 returns for it (up to three). Used by case-insensitive literal matching.
evidence: Callees are the confident Regex_NodeAlloc plus the generic list append (0x6E78D4/0x6E78EC); the loop over the alternatives returned by 0x513F78 is the only thing the body does besides the single tagged push, matching the name.

name: Regex_OpPushValueTaggedByte
signature: u32 Regex_OpPushValueTaggedByte(RegexCursor* cursor, RegexSet** out, RegexSet** target)
summary: Pushes one value into the result list using tag type 4 (an 8-bit payload taken from the instruction's +0xA byte). Returns 0/2.
evidence: Allocates through the confident Regex_NodeAlloc and appends through 0x6E78A4; the 22-line body is the same shape as the two PushValue opcodes, differing only in the tag constant, so the handler role is established.

name: Regex_Set_Intersect
summary: Intersects two sorted character-range lists in place: keeps only the overlap of the first list, trimming or dropping intervals the second list does not cover. Returns 1 when the list still has ranges, else 0.
evidence: Called by the confident Regex_State_SplitOverlappingClasses (0x512928) and Regex_MatchNode (0x510EB8) as a pure set operation, and it sits in the same function family as the already-confident Regex_Set_Subtract / Regex_Set_AddRange / Regex_Set_Normalize (0x513648/0x51384C/0x513A38) using the same alloc/free pair 0x51435C/0x514390.

name: maybe_Snd_AdvanceFrameCounter
summary: Polls one audio-transfer slot: snapshots its sync handle (svcWaitSynchronization1), and when a full frame period (0x400000 DSP ticks) has elapsed it clears the pending flag, bumps the slot's frame byte and reports true; otherwise it reports false and leaves the slot alone.
evidence: New named callers are the audio waiters Snd_WaitAudioTransfer (0x517884) and Sound_GetDisplayTime / Sound_WaitForDisplayTime, which is exactly a per-transfer frame tick; nothing in the body counts graphics frames, so the 'frame counter' wording is kept for the transfer frame rather than renamed.

name: maybe_Snd_ResetFrameCounter
summary: Unconditional twin of maybe_Snd_AdvanceFrameCounter: takes the slot's sync handle, clears the pending flag and bumps the byte counter beside the slot without testing whether a frame period elapsed. Used when a waiter restarts its timing.
evidence: Same named caller set as 0x5191B4 (Snd_WaitAudioTransfer, Sound_GetDisplayTime/WaitForDisplayTime) and the same body minus the 0x400000 test; both are called back to back, so it is the force-update path of the same transfer tick.

name: Sound_WaveBuffer_ComputeLayout
summary: Derives a wave buffer's chunk pointers from its counts: converts the two float-derived counts with VectorFloatToUnsigned(...,3), spaces the chunks 0x280 bytes apart and fills the four mix-buffer pointers, then hands the result to Sound_WaveBuffer_BuildChannelParams.
evidence: The callee Sound_WaveBuffer_BuildChannelParams is a confirmed name now, and the callers are Sound_Channel_SetWaveBufferAux and Sound_Player_StartSlotTrackB - both take a wave buffer and need its chunk pointers, which is exactly what this body computes.

name: Sound_WaveBuffer_Reset
summary: Resets a wave-buffer descriptor to its default state (state byte 2, default command word, cleared counters and list head) and re-initialises its embedded sync primitive.
evidence: Its only caller is the confident Sound_Channel_InitSlot, which allocates a channel and resets its wave buffer before use; the body is a straight field-reset routine, so nothing about the guess was in conflict.

name: maybe_Sound_Channel_FlushPriority
summary: When the channel's command word has the 0x8000 'priority expired' bit set, tells the DSP to release that channel and clears the bit; otherwise does nothing.
evidence: Now called from the confident Sound_Channel_UpdateScheduler, which supports 'clean up after the scheduler picked another channel', but the 0x8000 flag is only inferred from the mask, so the priority wording stays provisional.

name: maybe_Sound_CloseStream
summary: Closes an open sound stream: if the module is initialised it flushes the stream through the sound service (Svc_Snd_Cmd002C), closes the handle and reports the result. Shutdown/error path only.
evidence: Still has no named caller outside itself; the only confirmation is Svc_Snd_Cmd002C (0x51AE60) being a confirmed sound-service wrapper, which fixes the subsystem but not the 'close' direction.

name: Gfx_Y2r_WaitForCompletion
summary: Polls the Y2R status command (0x00260040) until the unit reports the completion code that 0x51AF38 returns, and returns that result.
evidence: Its caller is the confident Gfx_Y2r_Convert (0x501300), and the sibling helpers Gfx_Y2r_SendGetStatus / Gfx_Y2r_IsBusy / Gfx_Y2r_StartConversion (0x51AF38/0x51AF98/0x51B088) now carry confident names, which places this in the Y2R polling half of the driver.

name: Gfx_Y2r_GetSessionHandle
summary: Reads the colour-conversion session handle with the Y2R GET_HANDLE command, closing any previous handle first, and writes it to *out.
evidence: Called from the confident Gfx_Y2r_Init and implemented by the confident Gfx_Y2r_SendGetHandle (0x51B04C); the svc 0x23 close before the request matches the handle-ownership comment in Gfx_Y2r_Init.

name: maybe_Sound_NotifyServiceThread
summary: Reads the current thread id and sends it, together with the global sound context, to the raw sound-service request Svc_Snd_Cmd001F. A 13-line wrapper with no other logic.
evidence: Svc_Snd_Cmd001F (0x51BDAC) is a confirmed service wrapper, so the subsystem is right, but 'NotifyServiceThread' is still a reading of the two arguments rather than something the body proves.

name: Fx_System_InitRandomVectorTables
summary: Allocates the two 512-entry vec3 tables (0x1800 bytes each) used by the particle emitter: the first is filled with xorshift128 random vectors in [-1,1), the second holds the same vectors normalised to unit length, and both are published through the globals at 0x7B0034.
evidence: Its only caller is the confident Fx_System_Init, and the sibling table builder Math_InitSinTable128 (0x5230B4) is called from the same init; both allocate from the same 512-entry pool, so 'init-time table setup' is now certain.

name: Math_InitSinTable128
summary: Builds the effect system's 128-entry sine table: for i in 0..0x7F it stores sin(i/128 * 2*pi) * 0.5 + 0.5, interpolating from the existing 256-entry sine table at 0x741AFC with 24-bit fraction, and publishes the table through 0x007B0030.
evidence: Called from the confident Fx_System_Init together with 0x51D3E8 (the random-vector tables); the 0x741AFC table it reads is the shared 256-entry sine table used by 0x125034, so the build-from-sine role of this loop is confirmed.

name: Gfx_ResourceSlot_ReleaseTwo
summary: Releases both resources held by the global slot pair at 0x7B0034 by calling the object's virtual release slot (vtable+0xC) once per word, then clears the pair. Same idiom as the single-slot releasers.
evidence: Its caller is the confident Fx_System_Shutdown, which tears down the tables 0x51D3E8/0x5230B4 allocate; releasing both published pointers there is the only consistent reading.

name: Gfx_ResourceSlot_Release
summary: Releases one global resource slot (the 0x7B0030 table allocated by Math_InitSinTable128) through its virtual release slot and clears the published pointer.
evidence: Called from the confident Fx_System_Shutdown immediately next to 0x51D5B4, and it clears the pointer that Math_InitSinTable128 publishes; the single-release variant of the same idiom.

name: Gfx_ResourceSlot_ReleaseArrayEntry
summary: Releases one three-word resource slot (destroy through vtable+0xC, clear owner and handle) and returns the slot. Used as the element destructor of the Fx system's 30-slot resource array.
evidence: Called from the confident Fx_System_Shutdown, which walks the same 30-slot array, and it uses the identical vtable+0xC release idiom as the two siblings above.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesFromGlobalVelocity
summary: Particle spawn loop that takes each particle's velocity from the global constant vector g_0051EB18 instead of the emitter's random table, clamps the spawn count with g_0051EB00/g_0051EB04, then hands each particle to the shared quad builder 0x51D5F0.
evidence: The shared builder is now the confident Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad, and 0x530798 (the node allocator) is named too; the emitter type that selects this variant is still only inferred from the call site, so the prefix stays.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomRadius
summary: Emission variant that randomises the spawn radius (one RNG draw, then the square root of the squared radius) before handing each particle to the shared quad builder.
evidence: Now that Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad is a confident name, the 'emit variant' reading is supported, but the radius distribution is still derived from the arithmetic alone and the function has no direct caller.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomOriented
summary: Emission variant that draws three random angles and multiplies them into a rotation matrix (0x12551C) so each spawned particle gets its own orientation before the quad is built.
evidence: Confident Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad callee plus the 0x12551C matrix multiply; the orientation reading is still an inference from the three angle draws, so the prefix stays.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRadialSpread
summary: Emission variant that spreads particles radially around the emitter axis: two square roots per particle (one for the radial offset, one for the height) before the quad build.
evidence: Shared builder is a confident name; the radial reading still comes only from the pair of square roots and the axis constants, and there is no direct caller to corroborate it.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRing
summary: Ring/disc emission: takes a random radius factor, scales it by (1 - distance/radius) and a square root, orients the offset with the 16-byte RNG table at g_005209A8 and writes the quad.
evidence: Confident Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad callee; the ring/disc shape is inferred from the radial factor, not from a caller, so the prefix stays.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesBox
summary: Box/axis emission: splits the spawn count between the X and Z axes with the LCG, offsets each particle along the chosen axis and leaves the other component on the centre line (no square root is used).
evidence: The shared builder is a confident name; the box shape is still read off the two-axis split in the body, with no named caller to confirm the emitter type.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesSphere
summary: Spherical-shell emission: computes the radius as sqrt((1 - r) + r^2*(1 - r)) so particles land on the emitter's sphere surface, then builds the quad.
evidence: Confident Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad callee; the sphere formula is a body reading only, so the name stays provisional.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesOriented
summary: Fully oriented emission: builds a 4x4 basis from the three stored angles, optionally rotates the particle direction with 0x12551C and writes the quad. Supports an alternate orientation source.
evidence: Confident shared quad builder and the 0x12551C multiply; the 'oriented' reading is an inference from the matrix build, not a caller-confirmed emitter type.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesCone
summary: Cone emission: the radial factor is r + (1-r)*(1 - distance^2), giving a density that falls off towards the cone base, then each particle goes through the shared quad builder.
evidence: Shared builder Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad is a confident name, but the cone shape is still read from the falloff formula only; no direct caller names the emitter type.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesArc
summary: Arc emission: spaces particles evenly along an arc by stepping the angle with 1/(count-1) and emits them along the rotating axis; a single particle falls back to the base angle.
evidence: Confident Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad callee; the even-angle stepping is visible in the body but nothing external confirms the emitter type.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomB
summary: Emission variant combining one RNG draw, a square root and the shared quad builder; differs from 0x51F5B8 in the field set it initialises (it uses the 0x5227C4 distance bias).
evidence: Only the shared builder is a confident name; the suffix B exists because the body is a close copy of another variant, so the prefix stays.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomOrientedB
summary: Second random-orientation emission variant: one RNG draw plus a 0x12551C matrix multiply and two square roots; writes orientation-related fields on the particle before the quad build.
evidence: Shared builder confirmed, but the B/C variants differ only in which emitter fields they inherit, which no caller or constant proves; kept provisional.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomOrientedC
summary: Third random-orientation emission variant (one RNG draw, one matrix multiply, two square roots); differs from 0x522BA8 in which particle fields it inherits from the emitter.
evidence: Same body family as 0x522BA8 with a different inherited-field set; no external evidence distinguishes the two, so the prefix stays.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRadialC
summary: Radial emission variant driven by the emitter's lifetime accumulator: computes a random radius and writes the particle quad, returning an integer status instead of the usual float.
evidence: Shared builder is a confident name; the public wrapper 0x5307E0 that dispatches the float-returning variants was not followed for this one, so the return-type difference is unexplained and the name stays provisional.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRadialD
summary: Another radial emission variant: one square root per particle and a different RNG table, used by an emitter type whose distribution is a flat disc.
evidence: Shared builder confirmed; the flat-disc reading comes only from the arithmetic, no caller corroborates it.

name: maybe_Fx_AllocParticleNode
signature: u32* maybe_Fx_AllocParticleNode(FxParticlePool* self, FxParticleType* type, u32 flags)
summary: Hands out one block from the fixed pool at self+0x33C (round-robin cursor masked by self+0x45C), unlinks it from the per-type free list at self + type*4 + 0x340, stamps the flags word and returns it; returns 0 when the pool scan gives up after self+0x450 steps.

name: Fx_EmitterInitFromTemplate

summary: Resets a live emitter: clears the state words, stores the owner id at +0xDC, installs the default parameter block from g_0052B9BC and re-runs the module and spawn-transform updates.
evidence: Called from the confident Fx_SpawnEmitter right after the template init, and it re-runs Fx_EmitterUpdateModules (0x52Bxxx family); a reset/rebind step is the only consistent reading.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListL
signature: u32 maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListL(FxEmitter* self, u32 arg2, FxParticle* particle, int forwarded, u32 arg5)
summary: List updater for one emitter type: clears the +0x284 counter, applies the per-particle normal/state helpers (0x527738, 0x52793C) and walks the active list. The letter suffix is a disambiguator between template copies, not an emitter type.

summary: Simplified active-list updater: walks the list applying 0x523D0C, stops early when the emitter flag 0x400 is set, and decrements the list counters with 0x5209DC.
evidence: Body is the short variant of the family, still without a caller; the early-out on flag 0x400 is the only distinguishing feature.

summary: Active-list updater that combines the 0x52413C/0x52570C per-particle helpers with 0x526B98 and the 0x526554 emitter update. Letter suffix is a disambiguator, not a type.
evidence: Same family, same helpers as L/M but a different pair of per-particle routines; no external caller.

summary: Minimal active-list updater: walks the list calling 0x52413C for each eligible particle and counts the processed entries in +0x284.
evidence: 24-line body, still no caller; only the per-particle helper call is identifiable.

signature: u32 maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListQ(FxEmitter* self, u32 arg2, FxParticle* particle, int forwarded, u32 arg5)
summary: Dispatcher-style list updater: selects a per-particle helper by the particle's type/subtype fields and drives the main update 0x52C728. The common entry point used by several emitter types.
evidence: Body switches on particle fields and calls four different Maybe_UpdateParticleList* siblings, so 'dispatcher' is well supported, but nothing external names the emitters that use it.

summary: List update that reuses the main updater 0x52C728 for each particle and re-applies 0x524390; also reached from the dispatcher 0x52CD5C.
evidence: Called from the Q dispatcher, which places it in the same family; the letter suffix remains a disambiguator.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_ReleaseAll
summary: Releases every 0x3C-byte part record of a part list (count at self->f_C+8, records at self->f_18): frees each part's GPU blocks through Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock, optionally keeping the caller's part.

name: Ui_Widget_EnsureLayoutLink
signature: void Ui_Widget_EnsureLayoutLink(UiWidget* self, int layoutId, int arg3)

evidence: Its only caller is Ui_System_Shutdown, which argues for a UI-owned slot rather than the Gfx subsystem the first pass picked; the body itself only shows 'unregister + give back', so the subsystem stays uncertain.

name: maybe_Gfx_LoadTextureByName

summary: Loads a named resource from the loader (virtual +0xC) and parses it as a FLIM image through Gfx_Flim_Parse; returns the parse result.

name: maybe_Sound_StreamGroup_Init
summary: Initialises a four-slot stream/voice group: stores the owner id and re-initialises each of the four 0x10-byte sub-blocks with the 0x7FFFFFFF/1 'unbounded' priority bounds.
evidence: Reached only from Sound_Stream_SetSource (0x54260C), which is itself called by the confident Sound_AllocStreamSlot; the four-slot layout is clear but 'stream group' is still a structural name.

name: Sound_Stream_SetSource

summary: Starts a stream on an idle slot: initialises the four-voice group, marks the slot busy, stores the owner argument and the stream handle. The +0x85 guard byte prevents a double start.

name: maybe_Fs_ArchiveStream_Complete
summary: Drives a pending archive operation to completion: completes the current cached block with 0x504FEC and, when the operation finishes, calls the stream's completion callback (f_48) with the stored user value.
evidence: Its caller is the confident Sound_ArchiveStream_Open, which opens asynchronously and then services the request; 'Complete' describes the operation rather than the function's role, so the prefix stays.

name: Sound_WaveCache_Preload
signature: int Sound_WaveCache_Preload(SoundWaveCache* cache, u32 waveId, u32 size, u32 flags)
summary: Preloads one wave id: returns 1 if the entry is already resident, otherwise loads the raw wave through Sound_WaveCache_LoadRaw (flag 8 and no INFO block) or decodes it through Sound_WaveCache_LoadDecoded.
evidence: Callers Sound_WaveArchive_LoadEntry and Sound_WaveCache_PreloadFromFile are confident names, and the two callees Sound_WaveCache_LoadRaw / LoadDecoded are confident too, so the 'already cached? else fill' role is pinned.

summary: Second half of the decoded-wave load: allocates a 0x2C-byte header plus one word per channel, decodes the block, appends the per-channel offset table and writes the 'CIWV' trailer word.

summary: Preloads a whole wave group: builds the group descriptor with 0x5493C0/0x65EDC4 and then preloads every {id, size} pair in its table, aborting on the first failure.

name: Sound_Voice_SetOutputMode
summary: Sets a voice's output routing mode: forwards the mode to every stream of the voice and records it in the voice's mode byte; used together with the mute/loop setters right before the voice is started.
evidence: Three named callers now pin the use: Sound_SeqChannel_StartNote, Sound_Player_StartWave and Sound_SeqPlayer_StartMultiVoiceNote all set it immediately before starting playback, and the mode byte is the one the pan-matrix code reads.

name: Sound_Seq_NoteOnThunk
signature: void Sound_Seq_NoteOnThunk(u32 unused, SoundSeqChannel* channel, u32 note, u32 velocity, u32 duration, u32 reuse)
summary: Six-argument thunk that drops its first argument and forwards the rest straight to Sound_SeqChannel_StartNote; it exists so the sequencer can call the note starter through a uniform function-pointer signature.
evidence: The body is a single call to Sound_SeqChannel_StartNote, which is now a confident name (N_035), and the function has no direct caller - i.e. it really is a callback-table adapter, exactly as the name says.

name: Sound_SeqChannel_Tick
summary: Per-frame step of one sequence channel: moves the five envelope/fade counters (+0x8C..+0xA6) towards their targets, counts down the remaining-length counter at +0x7C and, while a note is held, keeps calling the channel's own vtable slot 1.
evidence: Now called from the confident Sound_SeqPlayer_ComputeTempoStep and from the play-frame loop 0x554xxx, which is exactly where a per-channel tick belongs; the body contains no other work.

name: Sound_SeqChannel_UpdateNoteTimeouts
summary: Decrements each note's duration counter at +0x190 and finishes the note when it reaches zero (unless it is already in state 4), then refreshes the note's gate flag.
evidence: Called from the sequencer play-frame path next to Sound_SeqChannel_Tick, and its helper Sound_SeqNote_FinishIfDone is a confident name. The decompilation is only cosmetically damaged (Ghidra lost the loop register as unaff_r4); asm 0x54E790 is a clean note-list walk: 'ldrne r4,[r5,#0x130] / ldr r0,[r4,#0x190] / subgt r0,r0,#1 / strgt r0,[r4,#0x190] / bleq 0x5565F8 / ldr r4,[r4,#0x1ac]', so the increment/finish/gate sequence is trustworthy.

evidence: Called from the sound command dispatcher (Sound_Command_ExecuteList) as the play command, and it sets the player state to 3 after registering with the driver queue - the start-of-playback path.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_SetParamBlock

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_CallChannelsSlot0
signature: void Sound_SeqPlayer_CallChannelsSlot0(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, u32 mode)
summary: Calls virtual slot 0 of every channel selected by a 16-bit mask, passing one argument. Slot 0 of the channel method table at 0x73D2E8 is 0x54EBA4, the pause/stop-mode setter, so this is the 'pause/stop selected channels' sound command.
evidence: Confirmed by the table contents: 0x0073D2E8 = 0x0054EBA4 (the channel slot-0 method) and the body's member-pointer decode on that table; Sound_Command_ExecuteList calls it as (player, mask, value).

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_FadeChannelNotes

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelField83

name: maybe_Battle2DUnit_DtorDeleting

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateScrollAnimation

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkDirectionC
